findings.description: The application uses `pickle.load()` to deserialize data from a file, which can lead to arbitrary code execution if the file content is controlled by an attacker.
findings.code_snippet:
tabversion = pickle.load(in_f)
        if tabversion != __tabversion__:

        self.lr_method = pickle.load(in_f)
        signature      = pickle.load(in_f)

findings.reasoning: The use of `pickle.load()` on a file stream (`in_f`) constitutes an unsafe deserialization vulnerability. The `pickle` module is not secure against erroneous or maliciously constructed data. An attacker who can control the input file can craft a payload that, when deserialized, will execute arbitrary system commands. The code performs no validation or sanitization of the data before deserializing it, making it vulnerable. All six reported lines contribute to this single vulnerability.

evidence.notes: All six reported locations are part of the same logical block of code and represent the same vulnerability. The core issue is the use of pickle on a file whose contents could potentially be controlled by an attacker.
evidence.code_context: The code opens a file handle `in_f` from a `filename` and then calls `pickle.load(in_f)` multiple times (lines 2009, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016) to deserialize parsing table data. This is inherently unsafe.
